question: Find the gain percentage, given that Siddhi sold her scooter for ₹31902 gaining (1)/(6)th of the selling price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given, Gain = 1/6 of Selling Price (SP).

Let SP = 6 units, then Gain = 1 unit.

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Gain = 6 − 1 = 5 units.

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of scooter = ₹31902

Gain = 1/6 of SP

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Gain

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5e6cd0e2494ea2b84a491134d54bca8c862dfe908300908624decd1c69360c5f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Gain = 1/6 × 31902

⇒ Gain = ₹5317

⇒ CP = 31902 − 5317

⇒ CP = ₹26585

⇒ Gain % = (5317 ÷ 26585) × 100

⇒ Gain % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Base of Profit and Loss

Profit and Loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless the question specifically mentions calculating it on the Selling Price.

General Formulas

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100
Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)

When Profit is a Fraction of SP

If profit is given as 1/x of SP, then CP will be (x − 1) parts. The true profit percentage will always be 1 ÷ (x − 1) × 100.
